title: Short-term market reversals and the S&P 500 index option returns (earlier draft: Implied Variance and Market Index Reversal)
one_line: When implied variance is high, the S&P 500 index, futures and SPY show strong daily reversals, mainly after DOWN moves, strongest around the close and open; a futures rule that bets against the last 30 minutes of the day and holds until 30 minutes after the next open earned slightly over 12 bp/day gross.

findings.statement: Negative serial covariance rises with implied variance and is driven by reversals of negative returns.
Reversal strongest in prices just after the open; very short-term reversal of the last 20-60 minutes most sensitive to high implied variance.
Futures strategy: position opposite to (and sized by) the last-N-minute return, close → N minutes after the next open; best N = 20-60; ≈ 12 bp/day for N = 30, gross.
Reversal stronger when S&P 500 option open interest is high (hedging flows).

why.pattern: Liquidity / fire-sale pressure at the close and option-hedging flows that unwind overnight.

reported_results.headline: When implied variance is high, the S&P 500 index, futures and SPY show strong daily reversals, mainly after DOWN moves, strongest around the close and open; a futures rule that bets against the last 30 minutes of the day and holds until 30 minutes after the next open earned slightly over 12 bp/day gross.

tradable_edge: New spec close_reversal_overnight_es: fade the 15:30-16:00 move, hold to 10:00 next day; condition on high volatility (AvgRange top tercile as VIX proxy).

decay_risk.reason: Gross of costs; ~12 bp/day ≈ 0.7 ES points at 6,000 — cost hurdle is close.

data_fit: ES 1-min Dec 2013 → Sep 2026, NQ 1-min Jul 2021 → Sep 2026 (2024+ protected in the backtest project).
